LESSON: NOAH AND HIS SONS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Bible
Topic 2.4: Noah and his sons

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Noah and his sons. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is the story of Noah still relevant in today’s society?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain five ways of showing respect to the elderly
2. respect the elderly at home, church and in the community

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: NOAH AND HIS SONS
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Noah and his sons helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: NOAH AND HIS SONS
Study Noah and his sons like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain five ways of showing respect to the elderly

What this means
In this part you learn to explain five ways of showing respect to the elderly. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain five ways of showing respect to the elderly.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Noah and his sons” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain five ways of showing respect to the elderly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Respect the elderly at home, church and in the community

What this means
In this part you learn to respect the elderly at home, church and in the community. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respect the elderly at home, church and in the community.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Noah and his sons in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respect the elderly at home, church and in the community. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Noah and his sons is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Noah and his sons” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain five ways of showing respect to the elderly)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Noah and his sons in your own words. (skill: respect the elderly at home, church and in the community)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Noah and his sons to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain five ways of showing respect to the elderly.
3. Practise this skill: respect the elderly at home, church and in the community.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Noah and his sons from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Noah and his sons: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Noah and his sons?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is the story of Noah still relevant in today’s society?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Noah and his sons means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain five ways of showing respect to the elderly.
5. Be able to: respect the elderly at home, church and in the community.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
